title: Path Existence Queries in a Graph I
summary: Given an integer n for the number of nodes in a graph, labeled 0 to n-1, and an integer array nums sorted in non-decreasing order of length n, along with an integer maxDiff, an undirected edge exists between nodes i and j if the absolute difference between nums[i] and nums[j] is at most maxDiff.
statement: Given an integer n for the number of nodes in a graph, labeled 0 to n-1, and an integer array nums sorted in non-decreasing order of length n, along with an integer maxDiff, an undirected edge exists between nodes i and j if the absolute difference between nums[i] and nums[j] is at most maxDiff. For each query [ui, vi], determine if there is a path between nodes ui and vi, and return a boolean array where each element indicates the existence of such a path.
constraints: nums is sorted, has length n up to 100,000, and max_diff is nonnegative.
Nodes i and j share an undirected edge whenever abs(nums[i]-nums[j]) <= max_diff.
For every [u,v], report whether the two nodes are connected by any path.
hints: In sorted order, a gap larger than max_diff is an uncrossable component boundary; every smaller consecutive gap provides a connecting edge.
Assign component IDs in one scan, incrementing after each oversized consecutive gap.
Build component[index] from component[index-1], then compare IDs for every query.
No edge can cross an oversized sorted gap, while consecutive allowed edges connect every index inside a gap-free interval.
editorial: No edge can cross an oversized sorted gap, while consecutive allowed edges connect every index inside a gap-free interval.

tests.explanation: A node reaches itself, but the gap of two separates nodes zero and one.
The initial gap separates node zero; consecutive later gaps connect nodes one through three.
